title: Intersection of Two Interval Lists
statement: You are given two schedules, first and second. Each is a list of closed intervals [start, end] (with start <= end) representing busy blocks. Within a single schedule the intervals are pairwise disjoint and already sorted by start. Return the list of every interval during which BOTH schedules are busy at the same time, written as [start, end] pairs. An overlap that touches at a single instant counts and is written as [t, t] (for example [5, 5]). Return the overlaps sorted by start. If the two schedules never overlap, or either schedule is empty, return an empty list.
hints: Both lists are already sorted by start, so you never need to sort again. Can you walk both at once with a pointer into each?
The overlap of first[i] and second[j], if any, runs from max of the two starts to min of the two ends; it exists only when that low bound is <= that high bound.

After recording (or skipping) a pair, discard the interval that ENDS first, because the one that ends later may still overlap the other list's next interval: advance i when first[i][1] < second[j][1], otherwise advance j.
